messages:
devon_cust: Hey team — after enabling response_format=structured + strict=true our app started getting parsing failures. Some responses are HTML login pages or an error page instead of JSON, which breaks our parser. Happening intermittently (~1 in 20). Using token auth. Example curl attached.

maria_support: Sorry about that, can you paste the curl you used and the headers you sent? Also which model/endpoint and account/org id?

devon_cust: curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"...","response_format":"structured","strict":true}'

maria_support: quick checklist — are you also sending an Accept header? If absent we sometimes fall back to html for some auth flows. Also confirm the token is valid (expired tokens can produce HTML login pages).

devon_cust: No Accept header set. Token was rotated yesterday but we double-checked it's valid. Repro steps: repeat the curl in a loop and ~5% responses are HTML (starts with <!doctype html>) and status 200. Parser chokes.

samar_engineer: thanks for repro. Two things to call out: 1) response_format enforcement is done server-side by checking Accept and the response_format param. 2) There is a known edge where an auth fallback returns a rendered HTML error/login page when the token is considered invalid by an internal service — that can slip through with 200 in some proxy cases.

samar_engineer: can you try adding explicit Accept: application/json; profile=structured and also check for 401/402 instead of 200? Example:

```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Accept: application/json; profile=structured" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"...","response_format":"structured","strict":true}'
```

maria_support: Also can you share the first 256 bytes of the HTML response when it happens? That helps us map which service rendered it. If possible include the response headers too.

devon_cust: Tried with Accept header — seems much better. No HTML in 200s after 2k requests. Still saw one 401 earlier that returned an HTML body. Pasted headers: 

HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 1423

(first bytes) "<!doctype html><html><head><title>Unauthorized</title>"

chris_sre: interesting — 401 with text/html suggests an upstream auth service returning the HTML error page. We'll correlate with logs. Can you also send the x-request-id from the response headers when it happens?

devon_cust: x-request-id: rq_0a1b2c3d

billing_bot: FYI: account 12345 had a failed payment yesterday and was temporarily moved to a limited state (should be 402 not 401), but that wouldn't explain HTML 401s. I'll confirm the billing state and share if any rate limits were applied.

maria_support: Thanks — we're going to escalate to runtime infra. In the meantime workaround: 1) set explicit Accept header as samar suggested, 2) treat any non-application/json responses as retryable with token refresh check, 3) log x-request-id and response body for us.

samar_engineer: action item for eng: investigate auth fallback path that renders HTML and ensure it returns JSON error payload with appropriate status codes when response_format=structured/strict. I'll open an internal ticket and link this x-request-id.

deploy_bot: incident created: INFR-2026-381 — auth-fallback-html-on-strict-json. Assigned to samar_engineer.

chris_sre: quick mitigation we rolled out: proxy now asserts Accept header when response_format=structured and will convert known HTML error pages into structured JSON with 401/402 code and a short message. Deployed to canary region.

maria_support: Devon — can you confirm if you still see failures after adding Accept header and the retry-on-non-json logic?

devon_cust: Confirmed — after adding Accept header and a small retry + token refresh, errors dropped to 0. Repro no longer happening. Thanks for the fast turnaround.

samar_engineer: follow-up: root cause was an upstream auth service template rendering HTML when the auth cache timed out. Patch replaces that rendering with a JSON error and ensures status 401/402. Will ship to prod today.

maria_support: marking resolved for now. If you hit any more issues, please reopen with x-request-id and raw body. :thumbsup:
